t: Any funds made available pursuant to section 101 for U.S. Customs and Border Protection may be obligated at a rate for operations not exceeding that necessary to sustain the numbers of personnel in place in the final quarter of fiscal year 2010. The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate on each use of the authority provided in this section.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the notification requirement is a participatory procedure, but the notification goes only to congressional appropriations committees, which are inside the federal government. The section otherwise just sets an obligation rate for appropriated funds. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate on each use of the authority provided in this section.

qwen_block.w: This section requires a federal official (the Commissioner) to notify congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so this is intra-governmental communication, not participation by outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress as participation.
qwen_block.s: The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate on each use of the authority provided in this section.

opus.w: This section sets a funding rate and requires the agency to notify the House and Senate Appropriations Committees. Those committees are part of Congress, which is inside the federal government, so the notice never crosses the federal boundary. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no one outside the government is given a hearing, comment period or right to sue.
opus.s: The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate on each use of the authority provided in this section.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Commissioner to notify congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this notification is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: The Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate on each use of the authority provided in this section.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying the Committees on Appropriations constitutes "participation" because it involves communication with an external body. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, reporting to Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
